meta.title: Design port: one role set, the agent's mark, and a conversation on every element
meta.goal_md: Port the design pass (claude.ai/design, *Agent mark and token setup*) into the real page: `plan.css` and `plan.js`, served and static, light and dark, with the same tests and screenshots the page has today.
meta.summary_md:
The design pass answered the eight problems from the first real review with one system: four colour families that never mix (neutral, status, action, agent), a mark for the agent that is the ask control, its presence, its avatar, and its working state, a thread card that is a conversation once a question is asked, and a bottom bar with two verdict buttons and an autosave line.

The stylesheet it produced (`artefacto.css`, 36 KB) keeps the page's class names where they exist and adds the rest, so the port goes slice by slice: tokens first, because every later slice uses the roles; then the mark; then the ask flow; then controls, the bar, and notices; then parity for the static export and the test suite.

Every slice ends with the browser tests updated, a screenshot in light and dark, and the golden regenerated.
key_points: **Roles, not colours** (`p-tokens`): status keeps rust, amber, green and is never clickable; action is a blue for everything the reviewer clicks; agent is teal for the mark, its replies, its presence. Rust on a control is a bug from now on.

**The mark is the ask control** (`p-mark`, `p-ask`): a ring around a point. Rest, working (the orbit), waiting, off. It sits beside Comment on every element, labels itself on hover, and becomes the avatar on the agent's messages.
**A question thread is a conversation** (`p-ask`): a persistent one-line input that sends on Enter, the working state from send to answer, and a line that says who will hear it.
**Two verdicts, autosave said out loud** (`p-bar`): *Request changes* and *Approve* as one group, the chosen one filled, and a *Saved · rev N* line so leaving is not losing.
**Vibe is a question, not a task** (`q-vibe`): the third theme swaps three font families the page would have to embed.
out_of_scope: Comments delivered live (that is `--passive live` in the re-plan; the bar copy has a batched and a live variant ready)
The index page and the posters (same tokens later, not in this plan)
Any change to the event protocol or the skill beyond presence modes

phases.title: Colour roles and themes
phases.summary_md: Replace the page's tokens with the role set from `artefacto.css` and re-point every use of the old accent to the role it belongs to. Nothing below names a literal colour.

tasks.title: The role set in light and dark
tasks.summary_md: `:root`, the `prefers-color-scheme` block, and `[data-theme="dark"]` take the design's tokens: neutral (`--canvas --page --surface --ink --ink-2 --ink-3 --muted --rule --rule-soft --numeral`), status (`--alarm --warn --ok` with inks and washes), action (`--action` with ink, wash, rule), agent (`--agent` with the same), `--brand` for the square only, `--focus` on action, radii and rule width as tokens. Every `var(--accent)` in `plan.css` is then re-pointed by role: chips and risk figures to status, buttons and links and focus to action, the ask control and the agent's text to agent. A unit test parses the token blocks and checks the contrast of ink on page, action on page, agent on page, and each `*-ink` on its fill, at 4.5:1 for light and dark.

files.note: contrast test over the token blocks

acceptance: `rg -- '--accent' src/plan/assets/plan.css` finds nothing
the contrast test passes for light and dark
screenshots of the kitchen-sink page in light and dark show no rust on any control

tasks.title: Chips and dots from status only
tasks.summary_md: `.pv-chip-*` and `.pv-dot-*` per status: high, blocked, blocking filled alarm; medium and in-progress warn; low, done, changed ok; open ink; planned muted; cut and declined muted with a strike; unanchored warn, dashed. The thread status chip uses the same classes. The stat figures go hot (alarm) only for risks and blocking questions.
acceptance: every chip on the kitchen-sink page carries a status class and no chip is clickable

tasks.title: The vibe theme
tasks.summary_md: `[data-theme="vibe"]`: the violet ground, pastel spray roles, 2px rules, zero radius, sticker shadows, and the three families Bricolage Grotesque, Space Mono, Bungee. The theme toggle gains a third position. Decided (`q-vibe`: yes): the three families are embedded like Newsreader and JetBrains Mono. The alternatives were embedded like Newsreader and JetBrains Mono (about 400 KB more per page), or system fallbacks (the theme keeps its colours, loses its type), or not shipped in v1.

files.note: embed the three families if q-vibe says so

acceptance: the toggle cycles light, dark, vibe and the choice survives a reload
a screenshot in vibe

phases.title: The agent's mark
phases.summary_md: One SVG, four states, three sizes. It is the ask control, the presence pill's glyph, the avatar on the agent's messages, and the working indicator. This phase puts it on the page where the agent is; the next makes it the way to ask.

tasks.title: The mark and the presence pill
tasks.summary_md: `ag-mark` (ring, core, orbit) with `is-working`, `is-waiting`, `is-off`, and `ag-mark-lg`; the orbit animates only when working and not under reduced motion. The presence pill becomes the mark plus a word: live, working, waiting, off. *Working* is a page-side state: an agent is attached and a question of this page's is unanswered. The pill's `data-mode` and title keep the tests' contract, with `none` renamed to `off`.
acceptance: the pill shows the mark in each of the four states
the orbit is still under prefers-reduced-motion

tasks.title: Avatars, actors, and no ids
tasks.summary_md: Each thread message gets `pv-avatar`: the mark on its wash for the agent, a small ink square for the reviewer. The actor label stays for screen readers and as the small mono caption. Decided (`q-ids`: remove it): the thread id (`c-3`) leaves the page entirely; it stays as `data-thread` on the node for the agent's commands and nothing else. The head shows the kind label, the status chip, blocking, and a *when* on the right.
acceptance: no visible text on the page matches `c-[0-9]+`
an agent message and a reviewer message carry different avatars

tasks.title: The thread card by kind and status
tasks.summary_md: `.thread[data-kind=comment|question]` and `[data-status]` drive the left border: agent for a question, alarm when blocking, ok when changed, rule when declined, warn dashed when unanchored. The agent's resolution note becomes `thread-resolution` with the chip inline, instead of one more message. The unanchored target line links to nothing but says where it was.
acceptance: a resolved thread shows one resolution line with the chip, not an extra message
each status and kind is visible in a screenshot of the kitchen-sink page with seeded threads

phases.title: Ask and answer as a conversation
phases.summary_md: The mark beside every Comment button, the working state from send to answer, and a persistent input once a conversation exists. This is the phase the reviewer asked for.

tasks.title: The ask control is the mark
tasks.summary_md: `ask-btn` becomes a 1.75rem square holding the mark in the agent colour, with the label *Ask the agent* rising on hover and focus (`::after`), filled on hover. `is-labelled` keeps the text for the bar and for the first sighting on a page (the label shows until the reviewer has asked once, per browser, stored on first ask). `has-thread` tints the control on an element that already has a question. Acceptance rows use it icon-only as now.
acceptance: every element with Comment has the mark beside it
the label is visible on hover and by keyboard focus
after the first question on this browser the label is gone from the element rows and stays in the bar

tasks.title: The working state
tasks.summary_md: From the moment a question is accepted by the server until an agent message lands in that thread (or the page-level panel), the thread shows a working row (`thread-msg.is-working`: the mark orbiting, *thinking…* in italics) and the pill says working. If no agent holds the lease the row says *waiting for an agent* with the mark off. After two minutes without an answer the row says *still waiting* and stops orbiting. State is page-side and survives a body swap.

files.note: pending questions per thread; renderThread; presence
ask → working row → reply lands → row gone; no agent → waiting

acceptance: a question shows the working row within one frame of the server's accept
the agent's reply removes it
with no agent attached the row says waiting and the pill is off

tasks.title: The persistent input
tasks.summary_md: A question thread carries `thread-composer` always: the mark, a one-line input that grows, *Enter* sends, *Shift+Enter* breaks a line, a quiet Send button in the agent colour. No Ask button, no two clicks. A comment thread keeps Reply as a quiet button plus the mark to ask; asking there switches the composer into the agent colour. Drafts in the input survive a body swap the way composers do today (same draft store, kind `ask`, thread set).

files.note: openComposer / draftTarget / commandFor for the persistent kind

acceptance: a follow-up typed into a question thread and sent with Enter wakes the agent (`chat.sent` with the thread)
the input keeps its draft across a push
a comment thread still sends a passive Reply and an active Ask

tasks.title: Who will hear it
tasks.summary_md: `composer-presence` under a first question and `thread-noagent` in a thread say, with the mark's state, whether an agent hears it now or the question waits. The bar's hint and the banner read the same presence, so *reaches the agent now* is never said when nobody holds the lease.
acceptance: with the lease expired, every place that promised *now* says *will wait*

phases.title: Buttons and controls
phases.summary_md: One button family in the action colour, outlined; the only filled control on the page is the verdict the reviewer chose.

tasks.title: The pv-btn family
tasks.summary_md: `pv-btn` with `is-primary`, `is-filled`, `is-quiet`, `is-lg`, `is-agent`, `is-alarm`; the comment button, the reviewed toggle (action when checked), the composer's Add and Cancel, the thread actions, the expand and collapse links, and the theme toggle all become instances. `pv-textbtn` goes.
acceptance: `rg pv-textbtn src` finds nothing
exactly one `is-filled` control is on the served page at a time

tasks.title: Criterion rows
tasks.summary_md:
The actions row on an acceptance criterion: icon-only, shown on hover, focus, or when the row has a thread (`has-thread`), with room for both controls.

Built without `has-thread` on a criterion row: threads hang on the task, not the criterion, so a row cannot know it has one. The row keeps its controls on hover and focus.
acceptance: a criterion with a thread keeps its controls visible without hover

tasks.title: The comment composer's foot
tasks.summary_md: `comment-box` with a foot row: the blocking toggle (alarm when checked) on the left, Add and Cancel on the right as `pv-btn`s. The answer composer is the same box without the toggle.
acceptance: the blocking toggle turns alarm when checked and the composer's border stays action

phases.title: The bottom bar and the end of a review
phases.summary_md: Two verdict buttons instead of a checkbox and a button, an autosave line, and counts that go alarm only for blocking. The Approve checkbox and the green Send button go.

tasks.title: The bar's layout
tasks.summary_md: `feedback-bar` in two rows: `feedback-bar-hint` (the mark, one sentence, Got it) and `feedback-bar-main` with `feedback-bar-state` (*Saved · rev 4* with a dot; `is-saving` while a command is in flight), `feedback-bar-counts` (threads, reviewed, blocking in alarm), and `feedback-bar-actions` (the labelled ask, the verdict group). The bar wraps instead of clipping at narrow widths.
acceptance: the state line shows *Saving* during a command and *Saved · rev N* after
a blocking count is the only alarm text in the bar

tasks.title: Request changes and Approve
tasks.summary_md: `feedback-bar-verdict`: two `pv-btn`s in one bordered group. *Request changes* sends `review.submit` with `request_changes`; *Approve* with `approve`. The chosen one is filled after the send; the sent notice and the *Sent* dot follow. The server's `settle_verdict` keeps its rule that a blocking comment forces `request_changes`, and the static export's clipboard button gains the same two choices. Decided (`q-empty-request`): *Request changes* stays enabled with nothing written; it is a verdict on the plan, not on the comments.

files.note: settle_verdict with the two explicit verdicts

acceptance: Approve delivers `verdict: approve`; Request changes delivers `request_changes`
after a send the chosen button is filled and the bar says Sent
no Approve checkbox exists

tasks.title: Leaving is not losing
tasks.summary_md: The first time a page has unsent work and the tab is about to be hidden or closed, the state line reads *Saved. The agent sees your notes when you send them.* for a moment; no confirm dialog, nothing blocks. The banner's three steps end with *send, or come back later*.
acceptance: hiding the tab with unsent work updates the state line; a reload shows the same threads and answers

phases.title: Notices
phases.summary_md: One component for everything the page says on its own: the agent's nudge, the agent stopped, no agent attached, a new revision arrived, the review was sent.

tasks.title: pv-notice by kind
tasks.summary_md: `pv-notice[data-kind=nudge|stopped|noagent|revision|sent]` with the mark, a kicker, text, and optional actions (*Show what changed* on a revision, *Dismiss*). The nudge banner, the sent notice, the stop notice, and the reconnect notice all render through it. The revision notice is new: it names the revision and how many threads it resolved.

files.note: notices() replaces sentNotice / nudge / stop rendering

acceptance: each kind renders once with its border colour
a push shows a revision notice that names the resolved threads

phases.title: Parity and proof
phases.summary_md: The static export, the print stylesheet, the test suite, the screenshots, and the record.

tasks.title: The static export in the same system
tasks.summary_md: The static page mounts the same buttons, chips, bar, and comment box, minus the mark (no agent): the clipboard button becomes the verdict group's static twin. The print stylesheet hides the bar, the marks, and the composers.
acceptance: the static self-test passes and a static screenshot matches the served one minus the mark

tasks.title: The suite and the screenshots
tasks.summary_md: Every browser test that named a class or a text the port changed is updated with the slice that changed it, never after. This task is the final pass: the full gate, three screenshots of the kitchen-sink page (light, dark, and vibe if shipped) with seeded threads of every kind and status, and a static one.
acceptance: `cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --all` green
the screenshots are in `target/screenshots/` and linked from the record

tasks.title: The record
tasks.summary_md: `docs/BUILD-STATUS.md` gets the port's section: what changed per slice, what the screenshots found, the mutations, the review round. Spec 4.3 names the presence modes and the two verdict buttons; the skill's reference lists the `working` mode.
acceptance: a reader of the record can find every screenshot and every decision from `q-*`

risks.title: The browser suite encodes the old page
risks.mitigation_md: 65 tests name classes and texts (`.feedback-bar-chat`, *Send review*, *Mark reviewed*, `.thread-reply`, pill text). Each slice updates the tests it breaks before it is called done; a slice that leaves the suite red is not committed.

risks.title: Two buttons over three verdicts
risks.mitigation_md: The server keeps `approve | comment | request_changes` and its settle rule; the page sends the two explicit verdicts, and `comment` stays for the static flow and old pages. A server test pins the mapping.

risks.title: Vibe's fonts weigh about 400 KB per page
risks.mitigation_md: `q-vibe`. Embedding is the honest way to ship it; system fallbacks keep the colours only.

risks.title: Static export drifts from served
risks.mitigation_md: `t-static` mounts the same components; the static self-test and a screenshot pin it.

risks.title: A working state that never ends
risks.mitigation_md: Timeboxed to two minutes, then *still waiting*; cleared by any agent message in the thread and by a lease going off.

open_questions.question_md: Ship the vibe theme in this port? With the three families embedded (about 400 KB more per page), with system fallbacks (colours only), or leave it for later?
Should *Request changes* be enabled when nothing is written? The design leaves it enabled; disabling it until there is a comment or an answer would make the two buttons mean what they say.
Thread ids like `c-3`: gone from the page entirely (kept in the DOM for the agent), or shown in the head's tooltip?
The bar's copy has a batched and a live variant. Batched stays the default until `--passive live` exists; confirm, or make live the goal of the next plan.
